labels.name: P1
labels.description: High — major feature broken, no workaround

items.body:
### Summary

In the `anthropic_messages` transport, `normalize_response()` only promotes a tool call when the provider returns a structured `tool_use` content block. When the model emits the tool-call markup into a **`text` block** instead (i.e. the serving layer did not promote it to `tool_use`), Hermes returns `tool_calls=None` with `finish_reason="stop"`. The agent loop then treats the turn as a final answer and **halts without executing the tool**.

This is the same class of problem the existing VolcEngine workaround in `_repair_tool_call` already defends against ("provider leaked malformed tool data, recover defensively") — but at the response-normalization layer rather than the tool-name layer.

### Where

`agent/transports/anthropic.py` → `AnthropicTransport.normalize_response()`

The method iterates `response.content` and collects `tool_use` blocks into `tool_calls`, but has no fallback for the case where a complete `invoke` block lands in a `text` block. Both the streaming (`stream.get_final_message()`) and non-streaming paths funnel through this single method, so the gap affects both.

### Steps to reproduce

1. Use `provider: anthropic` (`api_mode=anthropic_messages`).
2. Drive a turn where the model emits a complete tool-call block as plain text (observed intermittently with some Claude builds, e.g. when the namespace prefix on the invoke markup is dropped so the serving layer cannot promote it to `tool_use`).
3. The API returns a single `text` content block with `stop_reason="end_turn"` and **no** `tool_use` block.

### Expected

Hermes recovers the embedded tool call and continues the agent loop (executes the tool).

### Actual

`normalize_response()` produces `tool_calls=None`, `finish_reason="stop"`. The agent loop ends the turn as if the model gave a final answer — the tool is never run. Multi-step / dependency-chained tasks stall silently.

### Proposed fix

Add a defensive salvage path to `normalize_response()`: when there are **zero** structured `tool_calls` but the joined text carries a **complete** invoke block, extract the tool name + parameters, re-promote them to real `ToolCall`s, re-map `finish_reason` to `tool_calls`, and strip the raw markup from the user-visible text.

Safety properties:
- Only fires when structured `tool_calls` is empty — the healthy path pays nothing.
- Only salvages **complete** blocks (closing tag required) — a truncated/streaming tail is left untouched so a partial call is never executed.
- Parameter values are run through `json.loads` so `"61"` → `61`, `"true"` → `True`, mirroring what a structured `tool_use` block would have carried; non-JSON values (paths, shell commands) stay as trimmed strings.
- Genuine final text answers are unaffected (no invoke markup → no change).

A PR implementing this with unit + integration coverage follows.

items.body:
### Problem or Use Case

# WhatsApp Group Sending with Hermes Skill (Termux) ג€” One-File Guide

This guide contains everything in one copy-paste-friendly file: problem summary, fixes, corrected files, install steps, tests, and GitHub notes.

## Overview

This setup lets Hermes send WhatsApp messages to groups through a custom Hermes skill called `wa-groups`, using an external Node.js script (`send.js`) wrapped by a Bash script (`send-group.sh`) in Termux.

## What Was Broken

1. The `wa-groups` skill existed, but WhatsApp/Hermes did not always load it.
2. The original `SKILL.md` had formatting issues.
3. The wrapper script used a wrong hardcoded path:
   ```bash
   /root/whatsapp-sender/send.js
   ```
   which does not exist in Termux.
4. `send.js` expects a full WhatsApp group JID:
   ```text
   <group_id>@g.us
   ```
   not just a numeric group ID.

## Correct Paths in Termux

Hermes skill path:

```bash
~/.hermes/skills/wa-groups/SKILL.md
```

Full Termux path:

```bash
/data/data/com.termux/files/home/.hermes/skills/wa-groups/SKILL.md
```

Wrapper script path:

```bash
~/.hermes/skills/wa-groups/scripts/send-group.sh
```

Node sender path:

```bash
/data/data/com.termux/files/home/whatsapp-sender/send.js
```

## Correct `SKILL.md`

Copy this into:

```bash
~/.hermes/skills/wa-groups/SKILL.md
```

```markdown
---
name: wa-groups
description: Send WhatsApp messages to any group via an external Baileys shell wrapper. Use this when a user gives a WhatsApp group number and asks to send a message.
version: 1
```

items.body:
### Bug Description

**Describe the bug**
The desktop app (Electron, remote gateway mode) crashes with
`RangeError: Maximum call stack size exceeded` in the `UserMessage` component
whenever I attach and send a photo in the chat.

After the crash the app is stuck in a crash loop on every restart, because it
auto-loads the session containing the photo and tries to re-render it. The app
only becomes usable again after the session is deleted on the server.

**Likely cause**
The attached image is embedded as a very large base64 data URI in the user
message. Rendering this huge string in UserMessage appears to trigger unbounded
recursion (markdown/syntax processing) and overflows the call stack.

**Environment**
- Desktop client v0.16.0, connected to a self-hosted remote gateway (basic auth)
- Backend v0.16.0
- Affected bundles: both index-mGKaPVL4.js and (after auto-update) index-CqhgUV32.js
- Vision model configured server-side (Gemini) — server side works fine

**To reproduce**
1. Attach a photo in the desktop chat and send it
2. UserMessage render recurses until the stack overflows
3. App crashes and re-crashes on restart until the session is deleted

**Expected behavior**
Image attachments (large base64 data URIs) should render without unbounded
recursion — e.g. render the image element directly instead of passing the data
URI through the text/markdown renderer.

**Workaround**
Delete the offending session on the server: `hermes sessions delete <id>`.
Sending photos via the Telegram integration works fine.

### Steps to Reproduce

1. Open the desktop app connected to a remote gateway (basic auth)
2. In the chat, attach a photo and send it
3. The UserMessage component fails to render the large base64 image data
4. Error appears: RangeError: Maximum call stack size exceeded (in UserMessage)
5. The app crashes and keeps crashing on every restart, because it auto-loads
   the session containing the photo
6. The app only recovers after deleting that session on the server
   (hermes sessions delete <id>)

### Expected Behavior

The photo should be sent and displayed normally: the UserMessage component should
render the image as an actual image element, without crashing.

Large base64 image data URIs should not be passed through the recursive
text/markdown renderer. They should be rendered directly (or truncated/streamed)
so that rendering an attachment never causes unbounded recursion or a stack overflow.

The agent should then analyze the photo (server-side vision works correctly), and
the app should remain stable on subsequent restarts.

### Actual Behavior

The desktop app immediately crashes to an error screen ("Something broke in the
interface") with the message "Maximum call stack size exceeded". The crash occurs
in the UserMessage component while rendering the photo message.

After the crash the app is stuck in a loop: on every restart it reconnects to the
remote gateway, auto-loads the session containing the photo, tries to re-render it,
and crashes again. It only becomes usable after the session is deleted on the server.

Full error output (top frames):

RangeError: Maximum call stack size exceeded
  [error-boundary:root] RangeError: Maximum call stack size exceeded
    at qge (.../dist/assets/index-mGKaPVL4.js:60:4141)
    at UserMessage (<anonymous>)
    at .../dist/assets/index-mGKaPVL4.js (UserMessage render)
  (same crash also occurs after auto-update, in bundle index-CqhgUV32.js)

[renderer] render-process-gone reason=killed exitCode=1

## Feature Request

Add UI zoom/scale controls for the desktop app.

## Problem

The default font size and UI elements are too small on some displays, making it hard to read and interact with the interface. Users with high-DPI screens or vision needs have no way to adjust the scale.

## Proposed Solution

- Add zoom in/out controls (keyboard shortcuts like `Ctrl+=` / `Ctrl+-` / `Ctrl+0`)
- Or a slider in settings to adjust UI scale (e.g., 80% - 150%)
- Persist the zoom level across sessions

## Alternatives Considered

- OS-level display scaling works but affects all apps, not just Hermes
- Browser zoom (`Ctrl+scroll`) doesn't apply to Electron/TUI apps

## Context

- Platform: Windows 10
- Runtime: Hermes desktop GUI app (Electron-based)
